name: Two Relative Wings Preserve Every Proper-Minor Sink Choice
statement: In the one-relative-wing inverse construction, suppose both sections peel to the overlap $O$ and every vertex of either section is an attainable peeling sink. Then every vertex of every nonempty proper pc-minor of the forbidden expansion $X$ is an attainable sink. Consequently no pc-minor of $X$ is a rooted factor.
proof: Each section is all-sinks by hypothesis, and the contraction peels to either section after clearing the opposite wing. For an old-coordinate elementary operation $\mu$, the overlap is the positive family $\mu O$, the sections $\mu B_i$ retain every sink by rooted-minor transport, and both relative wing orders transport. To end in one section, clear the opposite wing, delete the redundant copy of $\mu O$, and finish with the prescribed endpoint order in the retained section. Rooted transport extends the construction to all proper pc-minors. A rooted factor has an unattainable root, while $X$ itself is nonpeelable.
